title: Evaluate first-read activation and retained use
question: conversational behavior
prompt: Design the smallest valid evaluation for a revised skill description that should load at the first useful prompt. I need to distinguish: whether the natural description activates, whether the body is understandable on first read without undeclared vocabulary, whether a nearby prompt is handled safely even if the skill loads, and whether the method remains available on a later turn. Explain which claims need native activation, explicit body delivery, composition, or multi-turn evidence, and what a one-shot case cannot prove.

assertions.rubric: The response must separate first native activation, first-read body comprehension, declared dependency composition, nearby behavioral interference, and retained multi-turn use rather than treating `skill loaded` as proof of all of them.

The response must map native activation to natural description routing, explicit body delivery to first-read wording, exact composition to dependency claims, and stateful multi-turn execution to later retained use. It must state that one-shot evidence cannot prove retained multi-turn behavior.

The response must allow a nearby case to pass through either non-activation or harmless activation followed by a correct quick exit; it must not assume every nearby skill read is automatically a behavioral failure.
